EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Previews the Future of the Tenere Adventure Bikes With Mysterious 4 Concept
Tesla Wants To Build 1 Million Cybercab Vehicles a Year in Germany
13 photos
Photo: Tesla
Tesla is betting a lot of money on its German operation, where up to 1 million Cybercabs may be produced annually. Considering that robotaxis with two seats haven't established a large-scale commercial business anywhere on this planet so far, one has to wonder if Elon Musk is once again selling a vision ahead of the reality on the ground.
In any case, an estimated $3.3 billion is planned to expand Giga Berlin, a.k.a. the Grunheide factory. Tesla Cybercab production should begin there in 2029, and this investment could not have been announced at a more worrying time for the German automotive industry.
As you might have already heard, all three big German manufacturers are cutting jobs, reducing costs, and reconsidering their domestic production capacities. The Volkswagen Group, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW all blame Chinese newcomers and US tariffs, among others.
Tesla, meanwhile, is going in the completely opposite way with this investment. Betting that autonomous taxis will eventually justify an enormous manufacturing operation is definitely bold, and we already know that Elon Musk has lost a few bets over the years.
From the Cybertruck 's projected starting price and commercial success to the overly ambitious FSD timeline, the SolarCity bummer, and the jumping Roadster Gen 2 that has very little in common with the concept from November 2017, the guy has been wrong about many things.
If you ask me, the biggest problem with Elon's latest bet is assuming that Europeans will be allowed to use the Cybercab as intended by the end of the decade. There's also the matter of European legislators, who are frequently criticized both in the EU and outside it for being slow and reactive instead of proactive.
EU lawmaking does balance multiple institutions and different legal traditions, but looking at the bigger picture, the slower pace also prevents hasty mistakes while protecting the sovereignty of member states. As part of said €3 billion investment, Tesla plans a new production building at Grunheide.
Photo: Tesla The company intends to submit the building permit application before the end of 2026, as reported by Reuters. If the papers are in order and Tesla gets the go-ahead, construction should kick off in the first half of 2027.
Regarding the Cybercab's European ambitions, bear in mind that suitable regulatory permission and insurance arrangements are required. Tesla also needs an operating network and auto-driving software calibrated for the European market, where both the infrastructure and the drivers are different from those in North America. As of this writing, the Cybercab is exclusively deployed for autonomous rides in Austin.
Dallas will follow suit. The wider Robotaxi network, which relies mostly on the Model Y crossover, operates across metro areas in Texas, Florida, and California. Turning our attention back to Europe, Germany introduced a legal framework for Level 4 automated vehicles in 2021. Under said framework, operators must obtain approval and restrict operations to designated areas.
Fully autonomous Level 5 vehicles aren't yet covered by EU law, yet a new global regulatory framework emerged in June 2026. As of November 2026, those rules haven't been incorporated into EU legislation.
Given this information, the Giga Berlin expansion is built on two suppositions. First and foremost, Tesla expects to navigate both Cybercab approval and operational requirements by the time production is expected to start in 2029. Secondly, the automaker further sees a European Union where demand for the Cybercab has the potential to hit 1 million registrations per year.
Via // Reuters

Japan faces a difficult security environment. Relations with the rising superpower next door, namely China , are extremely tense at present and for the last year. Japan must also contend with a hostile Russia and North Korea as well. All three of these countries possess nuclear weapons and are actively adding to those arsenals. If that wasn’t enough, the second Trump administration has been distracted by the Middle East and also demonstrated a relatively carefree approach to traditional U.S. allies.
No wonder that nuclear talk is now fashionable among defense analysts in Tokyo.
Indeed, Japan has good reasons to take its defense more seriously and has set about doing so. For decades, Tokyo restricted itself to spending about 1% of GDP on defense, but that self-imposed restriction fell away in recent years. Today, serious calculations are underway regarding whether or not Japan should follow other middle powers like Australia and South Korea by creating a nuclear submarine program. While the idea is not without merit, Japanese and American strategists need to consider the wider consequences before stepping out on this new initiative.
In early November, the Chinese newspaper Global Times published an editorial revealing that China’s rather predictable reaction to any Japanese plan to build a nuclear submarine force would be extremely harsh. The editorial suggests that Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has “become obsessed” with acquiring nuclear submarines. The Chinese article is sharply critical of the initiative, explaining that it represents a “sleight of hand intended to bypass scrutiny.” It explains: “The fuel cycle, the reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel, and the management of nuclear materials associated with nuclear-powered submarines overlap significantly with the development path for nuclear weapons.”
This Chinese perspective interprets Japan’s strategy as follows: Acquire the submarines first, then obtain nuclear weapons — presumably following a secret roadmap by “right-wing factions.”
The same editorial also had harsh words for the United States, asserting, “The United States is well aware of this, yet it has long chosen to turn a blind eye.” According to this rendering, Washington leaders “seek to arm Japan, transforming it into a forward-deployed spearhead in East Asia and forcing it to shoulder a greater share of the costs of confrontation.”
The piece concludes that U.S. policy is “shortsighted and arrogant … [as it] gambles with the post-war international order and the nuclear non-proliferation regime, effectively allowing a dangerous ‘Pandora’s box’ to be pried open.”
The shrill tone of this editorial is worthy of note. China-Japan relations have entered a genuine crisis stage during the last year and Washington must be cognizant of the perilous escalatory dynamics, since it could unfortunately be dragged into an unwanted war between the two contending East Asian powers.
To be sure, there are reasons why Japanese nuclear submarines merit closer analysis. Not only is the Chinese Navy’s rapid growth altering the Asia-Pacific military balance, but Japan could quite seamlessly integrate into the existing AUKUS program, a Biden administration initiative from 2021 that unites America together with Australia and the U.K. to focus on jointly fabricating nuclear submarines.
Unquestionably, Tokyo does possess the requisite trained workforce and industrial capabilities to make such a force feasible, even in the near future. Nuclear submarines remain as a formidable naval weapons system – for sure. Finally, if the development of nuclear submarines can preclude the creation of Japanese nuclear weapons, that could perhaps form a sensible political compromise in this age of increasing insecurity.
At present, however, the counterarguments remain more compelling. Such a step by Tokyo would undoubtedly kick up a political firestorm both in the international community and most likely within Japan itself too. The Chinese editorial may be correct that opening “Pandora’s Box” and this route to nuclear weapons proliferation could initiate the much feared “nuclear cascade,” since many other countries may wish to go the same direction.
It’s also important to recognize that Japan already wields a very potent undersea force with some of the most advanced air-independent propulsion (AIP) diesel submarines in the world. True, nuclear submarines are generally larger and could carry a spate of new offensive weapons systems, such as land-attack missiles. But that would change the character of the Japanese Maritime Self-defense Force into a more offensive striking element, as opposed to a defensive force. A nuclear submarine fleet and associated offensive munitions (e.g. land-attack missiles) would soak up scarce resources for Japan’s crucial defensively-oriented, conventional forces and, moreover, much of the East Asian littoral has shallow waters that are not so amenable to larger nuclear submarines anyhow.
Most consequential, however, would be the obviously deleterious impact that this development would entail for China-Japan relations, as the above editorial makes clear. The sad but important reality of contemporary China-Japan relations is that this enmity is less based on divergent interests or aggressive intentions. Instead, the present hostility arises from dangerous, emotive historical grievances.
America cannot allow such unrequited nationalist impulses on either side of the East China Sea to escalate into a gravely hazardous “spiral model” of conflict. Therefore, Washington must reign in Tokyo’s ambitions for nuclear submarines, even as it encourages Japan to further develop defensive capabilities, such as air defenses, mine countermeasures, and base hardening consistent with the military lessons from the recent wars in the Persian Gulf and Eastern Europe.
Lyle Goldstein is director of the China Initiative at Brown University’s Watson School and concurrently serves as director of the Asia Program at the think-tank Defense Priorities.

EICMA 2026 • Honda CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports Is a Tongue Twister, Weighs Less but Offers More
Nissan Australia Reveals the Full Specifications for All-New Nissan Patrol Full-Size Adventure SUV
20 photos
Photo: Nissan
The Japanese automaker Nissan has been pretty busy in the Land Down Under this automotive fall season and wants to make sure the Patrol shines brightly among the other novelties.
More precisely, the local division of the Japanese carmaker has kicked off the autumn season with the celebrations for the 25 years of the X-Trail in Australia, which included the launch of the Rock Creek and 2WD e-POWER models back in September 2026. Nismo’s first performance center outside Japan opened in October in Australia, and the company also announced the all-new Nissan Navara Pro Plug-in Hybrid will join the Aussie lineup in early 2027 during the same month.
As far as the Nissan Patrol is concerned, during the middle of the month production of the new generation kicked off in Kyushu, Japan, with the first right-hand-drive Patrol vehicles rolling off the line at the Nissan Shatai with Australia as their destination. Also during the month, Nissan celebrated 60 years of Australian presence – and we haven’t even reached November yet.
Earlier this month, Nissan announced that, alongside Food Reborn, they developed the world’s first automotive exterior body panels made from natural fiber-reinforced plastic ( NFRP ) using fibers derived from pineapple leaves and also that it earned a tenth consecutive Gold Award for LGBTQ+ Workplace inclusion. Anyway, we finally reach the moment of the Patrol-related announcement.
Nissan Australia has confirmed the full specifications of the all-new Patrol for the local market and said that first customer deliveries are coming in December 2026. The grade structure includes six trim levels: Ti, Ti+, Ti-L, Ti-L+, PRO-4X, and Ti-L Reserve, starting from AU $106,361 (a little over $71k) and going all the way up to AU $155,241, which is around $104k.
The all-new Patrol can also tow up to 3,700 kg (8,157 pounds) braked, with up to 848 kg (1,870 lbs.) for maximum payload capacity. According to Nissan, the latter rating is higher than any competing models like the 2026 Toyota Land Cruiser 300 Series or 2026 DENZA B8. The PRO-4X is dedicated to serious off-roading, with an Adaptive Air Suspension in Off-Road Mode offering a 29-degree approach angle, 25.5-degree departure angle, and 27.5 degrees for the ramp breakover, with ground clearance rising to 271 mm or 10.66 inches.
The PRO-4X also has 20-inch black alloy wheels with 275/60 R20 all-terrain tires, while the Ti-L Reserve shares the Adaptive Air Suspension, and all models are equipped with full-time four-wheel drive, a dual-range transfer case with high and low range, an electronic locking rear differential, and eight drive and terrain modes – Standard, Eco, Sport, Tow, Snow, Sand, Rock and Mud/Rut.
Compared to the outgoing V8-powered Nissan Patrol, the new generation improves fuel economy ratings by over 15% combined, while all grades have more power – an additional 19 kW and 140 Nm or 25 hp and 103 lb-ft of torque thanks to the new iteration’s 3.5-liter VR35DDTT twin-turbo V6 packing 425 hp and 700 Nm or 516 lb-ft of torque.

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
GTA 6 Locked at 30 FPS: Not Even PS5 Pro Can Handle 60 FPS
78 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Now that GTA 6 is here , and pretty much the whole planet is playing it, the time has come to look at the game and figure out what Rockstar should have done better. One of the most debated topics is the 30 FPS cap, which for many people is unacceptable for a 2026 release, especially considering the hardware capabilities of new-gen consoles.
Not being able to run at 60 FPS is a limitation that has generated intense criticism online, with some people claiming they wouldn’t even buy the game unless Rockstar removes the 30 FPS limit. While I do have my doubts that those who love GTA will manage to stay away from the game just because it’s limited to 30 FPS, the criticism has made the headlines on multiple occasions, without Rockstar directly addressing it.
The time has come for the company to defend its decision for this highly criticized cap.
Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said in an interview that the 30 fps limit comes and not even offering a balanced mode that would increase the setting to 40 fps was a decision whose objective was to allow the game to handle the high complexity of every little thing that moves around you.
Chambers explained that the level of detail included in GTA 6 is so high and complex that finding the right settings doesn’t just come down to a toggle in your game menu. “The frame rate we’ve chosen gives us the right balance of presentation, simulation, and gameplay,” the Rockstar official explained.
With 30 fps enforced on all consoles, including the PS5 Pro, which at first glance would be able to handle 60 fps, is not supposed to offer the downgrade that many people might anticipate when checking out these specifications on paper. This is because it is entirely custom-built, meaning that Rockstar has found a way to deliver the smooth experience you’d expect without compromising what you see on your TV.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The more important part is that not even the PS5 Pro would have been able to handle 60 fps in GTA 6, and the reason is the same high complexity of everything around you in the game. Leonida is a vast world - the largest open world ever in a game - so the amount of information a console has to handle is enormous.
I play the game on my regular, non-Pro PlayStation 5, and I have to say that the 30 fps limit makes the gameplay feel as smooth and fluid as possible. I’m certain that a higher setting would have altered the gameplay, and after I tried playing it on a PS5 Pro, this thing became more obvious.
Sure, the upgrade from a regular PS5 to a Pro is easily noticeable, and I do admit that this is probably the best console to play GTA 6 today. I’m also seeing people complaining about the Xbox Series S, where the fps drop is more common, but everything seems to be running properly on the Series X.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution But at the end of the day, the PS5 indeed has upgraded internals, but Rockstar says it has preferred to use the graphics processors and upscaling technology specifically to “increase the game’s visual fidelity.”
Chambers said in a separate interview that GTA 6 is not like every other game that went live so far, so while on paper it might look like a latest-gen console like the PS5 Pro would be able to handle everything you throw at it, the new Grand Theft Auto is different.
“The complexity of simulating and rendering the environments and inhabitants in a world the scale of Leonida, while maintaining the density, visual fidelity, and player agency we envisaged, places extraordinary demands on the hardware,” he was quoted as saying.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The conclusion is simple, in his opinion: PS5 is not powerful enough to run the game at higher frame rates.
Without a doubt, it’ll be interesting to see how Rockstar handles all this high complexity once GTA 6 lands on PC. There’s still no ETA as to when this is projected to happen, but given the fast hardware ecosystem, capping the FPS limit wouldn’t make as much sense in the PC world. Unless Rockstar wants to make the game playable on as many configurations as possible, that is.
Previous reports on the matter suggested that the PC version of GTA 6 could go live as soon as 2027, with some sources claiming that Rockstar plans to keep it exclusive to new-gen consoles for at least one year.

Workforce reductions have hit over 1,000 biopharma employees in The Golden State year to date, with pink slips coming from small biotechs and large pharmas. Biotechs have been hit the hardest, with nine companies saying goodbye to at least half their staffs.
So far this year, 24 biopharmas have laid off or projected they will lay off at least 1,176 combined employees in California, based on BioSpace tallies. Of those companies, over 1 in 3 (38%) are pushing out at least half of their workforces, and two have shut down.
Biopharmas making cuts in California include AbbVie, BioMarin Pharmaceutical, Genentech, Gilead and Takeda. Foster City–based Gilead is laying off the most employees—193—counting the 108 people it let go in June at the Redwood City headquarters of wholly owned subsidiary Arcellx.
Of the nine companies eliminating most of their workforces, two wiped out all their staffs by shutting down: San Diego startup f5 Therapeutics and Oakland biotech Tempero Bio. The remaining seven biopharmas are making cuts affecting at least 60% of their employees.
Below is an overview of the nine companies’ cuts.
California layoffs ramp up as year progresses
While five of the biopharmas making significant workforce reductions in California announced or disclosed their moves in the fourth quarter, the layoffs began in Q1.
In March, f5 Therapeutics CEO Gary Choy posted on LinkedIn that the business was closing, noting that the past few years had been brutal for early stage biotechs. The shutdown likely affected a small number of people, as the company’s LinkedIn page at the time indicated it had fewer than 10 employees.
f5 was working on molecular glues developed with its proprietary NExMod platform, which used phenotypic screening to search for novel targets for previously undruggable conditions. Before shutting down, the company had identified 11 potential targets.
The next major workforce reduction, also a closure, happened in Q2. In April, Endpoints News reported that Tempero Bio was shuttering following a serious adverse event in a Phase 2 alcohol use disorder trial of lead drug candidate TMP-301. The company was developing the asset to address the neurobiological basis of addiction. Tempero CEO Paul Johnson did not disclose what happened with the study.
As was the case with f5, Tempero likely did not put a lot of people out of work with its closure. The company had between two and 10 employees in April, according to its LinkedIn page at the time.
Two large workforce cuts in California were reported in Q3, starting with San Diego–based aTyr Pharma. In August, the company announced it would lay off about 60% of its staff, which will likely affect around 30 people in The Golden State. The biotech made the move to help focus resources on advancing lead asset efzofitimod in interstitial lung disease (ILD), which causes inflammation and scarring in the lungs.
Workforce changes at aTyr included Chief Financial Officer Jill Broadfoot and General Counsel Nancy Denyes stepping down Sept. 30 and transitioning to consultant roles.
About a month after aTyr’s announcement, an Arsenal Biosciences spokesperson told BioSpace the biotech was laying off 99 employees, representing most of the company, across its two locations: its South San Francisco headquarters and Hayward site. Based on the most recent known headcount, the cuts likely affected about 78% of the workforce.
Arsenal’s layoffs were part of a strategic shift to focus efforts on developing in vivo CAR T therapies, even as the company explores strategic opportunities for its assets and technologies, according to a company announcement .
Fourth quarter workforce reductions, which number five so far, kicked off in October. First, Berkeley–based Caribou Biosciences announced that amidst a financing freeze in the CAR T space, it planned to discontinue further development of its clinical-stage pipeline, implement a “substantial” workforce reduction and explore strategic alternatives. The biotech is letting go of 87 employees at its lone location effective Dec. 7, according to a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notice . Based on Caribou’s most recent employee count, the layoffs may impact 90% of the workforce.
Strategic alternatives the biotech is exploring include, but are not limited to, a merger, acquisition, business combination or other strategic transaction involving Caribou and its assets, according to the company.

Here's Why You Won't Get Any Websites in GTA 6
78 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
GTA 6 has so many new concepts that the first few hours of playing the game come down to figuring out how to do certain things. But the part that’s missing - and which so many people seem to love, especially when playing online - is the World Wide Web.
Back in the day, when GTA 5 was still a thing - literally yesterday - players used to turn to their phones, load satirical websites, and do things like buying stuff online. It worked like a charm, because the WWW was already a part of our lives that we’ve gotten used to.
But it’s 2026, and GTA 6 is here, and we use websites much less. GTA 5 went live in 2013, when some of us were still using MySpace, so having a way to load a page on the Internet made sense. It doesn’t anymore, so the ability to check out a website in GTA 6 is no longer available.
In a recent interview , Rockstar Games’ head of development Rob Nelson explained the logic behind this decision: smartphones are still there in GTA 6, but the focus is now on apps and social media.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Theoretically, this means that we still have the Internet, only that we don’t have a browser to access websites. It might seem like a downgrade at first, but Nelson explains that this feature “didn’t feel necessary for us.” To be honest, I don’t think this feels necessary for anyone, as browsing webpages isn’t necessarily part of everybody’s daily routines.
Our lives revolve around apps these days, such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, reddit, and so on. Because GTA 6 was supposed to be more realistic than ever, embracing a similar approach just felt obvious.
“I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, ‘For what? What do you need it for?’ So, that was it,” Nelson is quoted as saying in the interview.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The Rockstar head of development explained that the team working on GTA 6 never made the decision to disable webpages directly. It came as a result of how the game was built, as the apps are already supposed to do everything players and characters in the game need.
And then, there’s the other part of the story. Without webpages, where you can buy stuff and waste time in the online world of GTA, Jason and Lucia graduate from what Rockstar’s employee describes as “robbing little s****y liquor stores and pawn shops” to bigger hits. This means you’re not stealing money from an ATM anymore and then pop up a webpage to buy a boat, but you’re now planning more sophisticated hits.
In some ways, this sounds like a way to focus on the actual gameplay rather than on side activities bundled with GTA that play a less essential role in the overall experience with the game. Additionally, it’s also a way to keep players off the Internet, as weird as that may sound, something that we - most of us already parents - are trying to do on a regular basis with our kids.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Eventually, GTA 6 feels like a natural evolution and progression not only of the gameplay itself but also of the mindset behind what you’re supposed to do in the game. Sure, it’s still a depraved world full of humorous nudity, but at the end of the day, many of the things you’ll find in GTA 6 directly resemble what happens in real life.
Rockstar doesn’t rule out the possibility of adding websites back to GTA in a future update. No specifics were offered, but Nelson clearly didn’t want to say a definitive no to a feature that people used to love in previous versions.
My guess is that websites could return when an online mode is added to GTA 6. The game is now just a single-player experience, while GTA Online continues to be based on GTA 5. Rockstar hasn’t shared any specifics on its online plans towards GTA 6, but considering this component will eventually go live, websites would make more sense at that point.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution This is because the online engine would involve buying stuff more regularly, so in addition to apps, having a straightforward way to purchase cars, boats, and houses with the money they earn in the game might feel more convenient. This might also depend on how people get used to the new system bundled with GTA 6, as many of those who’ll play the online mode will be players who’ve already completed the single-player experience.
For now, GTA 6 is all about protagonists Jason and Lucia feeling like they’re part of the world and becoming more than pickpockets who spend their money on beer when the day is over. So not having websites doesn’t feel like such a big downgrade when you look at the full picture.

Biotechs that announced series C financing this year and are hiring include one that secured $140 million and has locations in London and Massachusetts.
As biopharma job seekers create their target list of employers, they may want to consider companies with recent series C raises. This later-stage round of funding helps proven businesses scale growth through further development or expansion.
Here are three biotechs that announced series C raises this year that are hiring.
Triveni Bio: $65 million
Based in Watertown, Massachusetts, Triveni Bio is developing genetics-informed antibody therapies for immunological and inflammatory disorders, such as atopic dermatitis, asthma and eosinophilic esophagitis. The biotech prioritizes and targets primary drivers of diseases.
Triveni’s lead program is TRIV-509, a half-life extended monoclonal antibody for the treatment of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. In October, the company announced it has completed enrollment in a Phase 2 proof-of-concept trial for TRIV-509 and expects to report topline data by the end of 2026. Triveni also shared that it has transferred TRIV-920, a monoclonal antibody being developed for the treatment of pancreatitis, to a third-party biopharma focused on rare disease. It did not identify the biopharma.
In June, the biotech shared that it had raised $65 million in series C financing to support pipeline expansion and continued corporate growth. Specifically, Triveni will use the funds to extend the scope and rigor of clinical development of TRIV-573, a half-life extended, next-generation bispecific created to address the underlying cause of atopic dermatitis. Last month, the biotech announced it had dosed its first patient in a Phase 2 proof-of-concept clinical trial of the asset to treat moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
In other company news this year, Triveni CEO Vishal Patel was named a finalist for the Ernst & Young Entrepreneur Of The Year 2026 award. Patel was honored for his leadership and excellence in driving programs from concept to clinical trial with speed and rigor, the biotech noted in a press release .
Triveni is hiring for several positions in Watertown, including senior scientist, clinical pharmacology; director, medical writing; and senior scientist, translational research.
Ratio Therapeutics: $70 million
Boston-based Ratio Therapeutics develops radiopharmaceuticals for cancer treatment using its proprietary research and development platforms, Trillium and Macropa. The platforms harness the tumor-killing power of the alpha-emitting radionuclide actinium-225 to selectively destroy cancer cells.
The biotech’s pipeline of therapeutic and diagnostic assets target a variety of cancer indications. The lead program is [Ac-225]RTX-2358, a fibroblast activation protein (FAP)–targeted therapeutic. The asset is being studied in the ATLAS Phase 1/2 trial in patients with relapsed or treatment-resistant FAP positive soft tissue sarcoma, a rare type of cancer affecting tissues such as muscle, fat and tendons.
Ratio has partnerships with pharmaceutical companies Novartis, Lantheus and Merck. It’s working with Novartis on a therapeutic program and with Lantheus and Merck on diagnostic programs.
In July, the biotech announced it had closed a $70 million series C financing that will fuel its next phase of growth. Ratio expects to use the funding to advance its ongoing ATLAS study evaluating [Ac-225]RTX-2358 in advanced sarcomas and to move its next-generation radioligand therapy candidate into the clinic. The company also plans to expand its discovery pipeline into new, high-value oncology targets while strengthening its proprietary radiopharmaceutical technology and scaling its manufacturing capabilities to support pipeline expansion and future commercial demand.
Ratio is hiring a scientist/senior scientist, radiopharma development and tech transfer, in West Valley City, Utah; a facilities engineer in West Valley City; and a chemistry laboratory operations associate in Boston. The company also allows job seekers who don’t see a role meeting their qualifications to upload their resume and cover letter.
Basecamp Research: $140 million
Basecamp Research is developing medicines for diseases with limited treatment options by combining frontier AI models trained on proprietary biological data with technology for writing DNA sequences into cells. EDEN, the biotech’s first biological foundation model, powers three platforms spanning gene insertion, gene editing, and peptide and protein design.
Headquartered in London with offices and labs in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Basecamp has a pipeline consisting of early-stage programs focused on disease areas including oncology, autoimmunity and diabetes. Most programs center around large serine recombinases (LSRs), a class of enzymes that specialize in inserting large genes, Basecamp explains on its website . EDEN AI models scan broken genes to identify an optimal target site for an LSR, then design synthetic LSRs that can place a healthy copy of a gene upstream of a mutation to restore normal function.
In September, Basecamp announced it had closed $140 million in series C financing that it will use to train a new generation of EDEN models and advance a pipeline of AI-designed therapeutics toward clinical development. It will also use the funds to expand pharmaceutical partnerships.

Bentley x FRGMT Torcal Is a New Limited Edition Model
9 photos
Photo: Bentley
It’s been almost two months since Bentley pulled the wraps off its first-ever production electric vehicle, the Torcal , and the model has now stepped under the spotlight again with a new limited edition creation.
The British luxury automaker calls it “ the first bespoke commission for the Torcal, ” but that’s not exactly what this thing is, because it’s not a one-off creation. In fact, production is capped at 20 units for worldwide markets, and this makes it a limited edition model.
It does not have an official name, but the company refers to it as the Bentley x FRGMT Torcal, and it was made in collaboration with Hiroshi Fujiwara. The Bentley ambassador, who is “ a pioneer of Tokyo’s Ura-Harajuku streetwear movement, ” has collaborated with the automaker’s personalization division, Mulliner, in order to create this very special (looking) Torcal .
All units of the electric car are presented in the same Beluga solid paint, with a few interesting touches, such as the FRGMT branding on the front fenders and at the rear. These are joined by a set of 22-inch Vortex wheels, which have a black look and Anthracite Satin accents on them.
Photo: Bentley Additional highlights can be seen on the inside, where the special Bentley Torcal benefits from a combination of hides in Imperial Blue and Beluga. These are complemented by hand cross-stitching signed by the automaker’s artisans, as well as piano black veneers. Users are greeted by the “Bentley x FRGMT” graphics on the treadplates, which pretty much round off the makeover.
Bentley hasn’t said how many units of the new Torcal FRGMT are still available, nor how much this thing costs, but you can expect to pay more than the regular Torcal, which starts from over $220,000 in the United States of America. The Torcal S kicks off at more than $260,000, and for the First Edition, interested parties will have to pay in excess of $300,000.
Full production of the Bentley Torcal does not seem to have kicked off at the Crewe factory in the United Kingdom, and that’s not exactly a surprise, given that deliveries are expected to commence in 2027. The model is a zero-emission crossover that shares many nuts and bolts with the Porsche Cayenne Electric, as well as the smaller Macan Electric, and the Audi A6 e-tron, and Q6 e-tron, as all of them are based on the PPE (Premium Platform Electric) construction.
The standard Torcal has 810 hp (604 kW/821 ps) and 881 lb-ft (1,194 Nm) of torque combined, hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in 3.3 seconds, and topping out at 155 mph (250 kph). The Torcal S comes with up to 876 hp (888 ps/653 kW) and 996 lb-ft (1,350 Nm) of torque with Launch Control, drops the sprint time to 2.8 seconds, and increases the top speed to 162 mph (260 kph).

907-HP Lambo Temerario Spyder Is a True Work of Italian Automotive Art, At Least Behind the Seats
12 photos
Photo: Lamborghini
Lamborghini , as hinted and previewed and spied on countless occasions, has unleashed the Spyder version of the 907-hp Temerario supercar – and it’s a bit more than just a chopped coupe. Let’s see by how much more.
This week in November feels a bit overwhelming to me, frankly. I woke up on Monday, November 19, 2026, to a world of wrath over Jeff Bezos and his Amazon studio's decision to pass on an illustrious unknown for the role of James Bond. The 007 mantle now belongs to Robert Pattinson , who is not in his thirties, and thus we don’t know how many films he’ll be able to make; he’s also a true Hollywood superstar, not someone who can take the role and make it their own for a couple of decades.
The announcement arrived exactly 20 years to the day after Daniel Craig's debut Bond film, Casino Royale, and now the work is underway with iconic director Denis Villeneuve taking over the franchise. Also, AI fans know that Anthropic’s public trading starts today, November 19, 2026, on the eve of the Los Angeles Auto Show in California.
But, of course, more importantly, people are going crazy over the launch of Rockstar Games’ iconic title GTA, with Grand Theft Auto VI also coming out today in all regions. People have taken days and even weeks off to play the new title – and some want to have uninterrupted time and signed contracts with their spouses and kids to achieve that!
Photo: Lamborghini I don’t commit so much to virtually anything, but I appreciate them. Luckily for me, there were also some cool unveilings in the automotive space: yesterday Volkswagen unleashed the second-generation T-Roc R with 333 ps (328 hp) as their most powerful SUV in Europe – and it also has a rather steep price of around $66k at home in Germany, where pre-sales kicked off, you guessed it, exactly today.
Alas, if there is one thing that I want to go crazy about, it is the all-new 907-hp twin-turbo V8 plug-in hybrid Lamborghini Temerario Spyder. Spied, rendered, previewed, hinted, and teased on numerous occasions, this is the open-top version of Lambo’s ‘entry-level’ model. It remains a supercar in its own right, complete with the same power credentials as the coupe, but I dare to say that it’s way cooler.
First and foremost, at least from behind the seats toward the rear, it’s a true work of Italian automotive art because it’s not just a Temerario with the roof cut out – it actually improves on the pretty bland look of the regular model. There are no changes to the front, sadly, but if you look at it from above, like in the hero image in the gallery, it’s quite something to behold.
Photo: Lamborghini Now, let’s go over the specs from Lamborghini. Automobili Lamborghini has introduced the Temerario Spyder both in Sant’Agata Bolognese and Los Angeles in conjunction with the LA Auto Show and Mobility LA, with the new open-top sports car allegedly ready to reimagine the Fuoriclasse concept. The design belongs to Centro Stile Lamborghini, and the model only looks like it has a canvas roof – it’s actually a fully retractable hardtop.
How did they achieve the clean look? According to the company, the engineers and designers came up with a fully electric retractable hard top that employs a patented vertical stowing position. It has ten electric actuators, eliminating traditional electro-hydraulic circuitry. It’s not just a gimmick to make sure the price goes up by at least $50k.
Instead, the new vertical position of the hardtop roof behind the seats lowers the entire car’s center of gravity by three millimeters when opened, compared to the regular closed position, thus improving handling – but also “keeping weight distribution unaltered.” There’s also an electrically adjustable rear window that “allows driver and passenger to modulate airflow and engine sound inside the cabin.”
Photo: Lamborghini The Spyder has the same all-aluminum spaceframe as the Coupe , and compared to its predecessor, the Lamborghini Huracan Spyder, it comes with increases in static torsional rigidity (+6%), dynamic bending stiffness by 9%, and another 6% for the dynamic torsional rigidity. Compared to the Huracan EVO Spyder, it also has 50% fewer structural components and 80% fewer heat-input welds!
Behind the seats and the roof, when lowered, sits the 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 coupled with three axial-flux electric motors – one at the rear and two around the front, churning out a combined output of 677 kW or 920 ps and 907 hp, plus 800 Nm (590 lb-ft) of torque. According to Lamborghini, the all-wheel-drive Spyder can sprint to 100 kph or 62 mph in 2.8 seconds (2.7s for the coupe) on its way to a maximum speed of 343 kph or 213 mph, the same as its fixed-roof sibling.
Driving dynamics include the Citta mode for pure electric operation; there’s a three-level Drift Mode, increased cabin space compared to the Huracan EVO Spyder, the Ad Personam program offers up to 400 exterior paints, and audiophiles can select the 750-watt seven-speaker High-End Sonus faber Sound System plus an optional titanium exhaust system developed by Akrapovic, which reduces weight by 12% compared to the standard system. The longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the big takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) new “ World Energy Outlook 2026 ,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar.
The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran. Well-stocked oil inventories helped buffer the initial shock, and the IEA coordinated a release of emergency oil reserves. Some Gulf oil took routes around the strait. Atlantic Basin exporters shipped more, and China sharply cut its crude imports. Now more of the burden is falling on consumers, who are paying higher prices and cutting back.
“While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” said IEA executive director Fatih Birol.
EV sales are jumping
The IEA has seen EV sales jump in some countries hit by the crisis, along with increased trade in solar panels and batteries. For countries that import a lot of oil and gas, switching to EVs and heat pumps can help reduce their exposure to the next fuel price spike.

“The impact of Hormuz is only just beginning to become clear,” said energy think tank Ember’s chief analyst Dave Jones. “Hormuz will speed up electrification and renewables, likely faster than many people think. So much of the momentum for electrification at COP31 comes from the desire to have cheaper and more secure energy.”
Solar leads renewables growth in every scenario the IEA models, and nuclear power is growing strongly, too. Energy efficiency and biofuels could also gain ground. The push to use more homegrown energy could have a very different effect in parts of Asia, where some countries that import oil and gas have plenty of their own coal and could keep burning it for longer.
The world was already using a lot more electricity before the crisis. Since 2019, electricity demand has grown twice as fast as overall energy demand, outpacing global economic growth. Everything from industrial motors and air conditioners to EVs, heat pumps, and data centers is driving that growth. Electricity comes close to 30% of the energy the world actually uses by 2035 in each of the IEA’s exploratory scenarios.
How much oil could bypass Hormuz?
Before the crisis, around 20 million barrels of oil a day moved through the Strait of Hormuz. If shipping stays risky, new pipelines could route some of those barrels around the strait, while buyers turn to other suppliers or use less oil. In that case, the IEA says the amount of oil that needs to pass through Hormuz could drop to 8.5 million barrels a day in 2030 and below 2 million by 2035. The Middle East would still be the world’s largest oil-exporting region.
If the conflict is resolved, oil and gas supply could bounce back. A delayed wave of liquefied natural gas could also help bring prices down even as buyers refill their inventories. Faster electrification could take some of the demand out of both markets.
Cooling just overtook heating
The world is now using more energy to cool its buildings than to heat them for the first time, the IEA says. By 2035, the global population is expected to grow by 650 million and the economy by a third. Energy needs rise gradually in advanced economies, growth slows in China, and India and Southeast Asia lead faster increases across other emerging and developing economies.
Then there’s AI. Under the IEA’s Stated Policies Scenario, global data center electricity use doubles to 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030. That buildout is already running into grid and supply chain constraints, and in some places, local opposition. The IEA also flags risks to critical mineral supplies and threats to energy infrastructure from natural hazards and cyberattacks.
The climate math is still tough
Energy-related CO2 emissions stay around today’s levels under current policies. They start to fall under stated policies and drop further in the IEA’s Additional Response Case, which looks at what could happen if governments respond more strongly to the crisis. Even those deeper cuts fall short of what climate goals require. The current and stated policy scenarios point to 2.5C to 2.9C of warming, and the latest round of national climate pledges shows little sign that countries are speeding up energy-sector emissions cuts.
There’s a more immediate cost, too. More people gained access to electricity and clean cooking in 2025, but higher fuel prices and shortages threaten to slow that progress. Around 720 million people still live without electricity, and nearly 2 billion cook with polluting fuels or technologies.

Volkswagen Unleashes the T-Roc R High-Performance CUV With 328 HP, And This Is How Much It Costs
56 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The German automaker Volkswagen has revealed the new T-Roc R, with pre-sales of the model starting on November 19, 2026, with an MSRP of 59,995 euros at home in Germany, which translates to almost $66k at the current exchange rate.
The Volkswagen T-Roc is a smaller compact crossover SUV tucked below the popular Tiguan in the automaker’s lineup, just above the subcompact T-Cross. It’s generally regarded as the direct equivalent of the C-segment Volkswagen Golf within the SUV ranks.
The first generation launched in late 2017, almost a decade ago, and it was produced on the Volkswagen Group MQB A1 platform alongside a very long list of related models from within the group headlined by the Volkswagen Golf Mk7. The second iteration appeared in November 2025 based on the newer Volkswagen Group MQB Evo architecture, and it’s related to the Volkswagen Golf Mk8.
Just a year later, Volkswagen is also unleashing the second iteration of the high-performance version of the T-Roc. The original VW T-Roc R was introduced in 2019, featuring the same EA888 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine as the Golf R, pushing 300 ps or 296 hp and 400 Nm or 295 lb-ft of torque. Now it’s time for a successor, as previewed by our spy photographer partners on the numerous occasions they caught prototypes during testing.
Volkswagen has decided that only one year should pass from the launch of the second T-Roc, and the flagship model of the product line celebrated its world premiere online on November 18, 2026, with pre-sales at home in Germany starting during one of the busiest days of the year – November 19 marks the arrival of the eagerly-awaited GTA VI video game (13 years in the making) and the start of the LA Auto Show, while this week we also found out the name of the next actor playing James Bond.
Anyway, the all-new Volkswagen T-Roc R Mk2 uses the newer EA888 evo5 version of the consecrated engine with 48-volt technology, and the MHEV unit develops 245 kW (333 ps or 328 hp), making it “the most powerful Volkswagen SUV on the European market.” It can sprint to 100 kph or 62 mph in five seconds and comes with standard perks like launch control and the 4Motion all-wheel drive system.
Speed is electronically limited to the classic threshold of 250 kph or 255 mph, but VW says the T-Roc R will be “particularly agile at low engine speeds,” all thanks to an electrically-driven compressor driven by the 48V system, which is used for the first time in an R model. The AWD system also has R-Performance torque vectoring; there’s an R button on the steering wheel to activate ‘Race’ mode, and adaptive DCC sports chassis plus Special and Drift driving profiles are also standard. GTA 6: Watch the First Hour of Gameplay and the First Two Chapters
78 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
I’ve always hated giving spoilers, but GTA 6 is here , and you really need to watch this first hour of gameplay. It’s more of a movie than a game, as Rockstar wanted to make sure you get to know Lucia, Jason, their past, and how they ended up together.
I’ve never seen so many people loving to watch cutscenes, to be honest. Rockstar used the first two chapters in GTA 6 not only to introduce you to the game, but also to help you get to know the people that’ll guide you throughout this fascinating new adventure in the city of Leonida.
In many ways, GTA 6 starts just like a romance film, with Lucia and Jason getting to know each other when they are about to get arrested. Because I don’t want to give more spoilers, let’s just say that the story continues with Lucia being away from Jason, who continues to do things that you obviously shouldn’t do.
GTA 6 is another top-notch mix of ridiculous nudity, depraved life, crime, fantastic music, and everything else that we’ve grown to love for over one decade in Grand Theft Auto V . It’s almost emotional to be able to play GTA 6 after all these years, just to get the old GTA feeling in a completely modern and refreshed appearance.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Everything feels and is new. The cars - because we’re at autoevolution here, so we’re obsessed with cars - look much more realistic, and the control isn’t by any means as arcade-ish as it was in GTA 5. It’s obviously not Gran Turismo, but it’s very clear that developers have spent a reasonable amount of time to get this right.
The dynamic weather system that Rockstar is so proud of makes the game feel more realistic, but at the same time, it also makes driving more challenging, especially at night. The level of glare during night driving when it’s raining makes perfect sense, and anyone wearing glasses will tell you that Rockstar got this right.
The car crashes aren’t necessarily as realistic as I expected them to be, but you’ll get a lot of feedback whenever you collide with another vehicle. That’s a good thing because crashes are not supposed to be as common as they were in GTA 5. I mean, yes, they are there, and you can always hit another vehicle on the road, but you’d better not do this too often because it’s much, much harder to get out of a major fender-bender with the police on your tail.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Stealing cars is also more difficult than in GTA V. If you’re like me, you’ll probably rush to the first car you see out there immediately after you finish the first chapters and Brian gives you the first missions. You won’t be able to steal any cars from your neighborhood - you know, you’re supposed to be a good neighbor, after all - and most cars you see parked on the side of the road are locked.
The only option would be to smash the side window, much like the Kia Boys do in real life , but this approach will result in a police report that’ll have a patrol car sent after you in a matter of seconds. The car alarm will fire up, so you’ll better leave the area as fast as possible. Returning to the area after a couple of minutes, even if police are not on your tail anymore, is not a good idea because officers will continue to patrol the neighborhood and look for you.
Drivers show some resistance when you’re trying to take them off their cars and steal them. You’ll have to fight them, though this is quite easy, but if a police officer is nearby, that’ll get you into trouble. Truck drivers are obviously the most likely to engage in a fight, but aside from hitting you once or maybe twice, they won’t be able to stop you from stealing their vehicles.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Driving and listening to music while respecting the law continues to be ridiculously satisfying. I lost count of how many times I did this in GTA 5, and now that GTA 6 is here with improved graphics and mechanics, just driving around and listening to the fantastic tunes on the radio - often laughing because it’s still GTA and the people on the radio drop all kinds of references to real life - is a very relaxing way of playing this game.
I’ll drop a spoiler now. Lucia won’t be around for your first missions, and that’s why Jason shows up more, including when Brian sends him to bring home the checks. She’ll eventually be there, but now’s the time to grab the popcorn and watch the first hour of gameplay, which could very well be a Hollywood movie, considering the story and graphics.
You'd better not skip the cutscenes when you start playing GTA 6. Meanwhile, I'm already working on the full review, so stay tuned for the full details.
